All nineteen remain unqualified physical routes. The eight GND number-to-signal assignments are arbitrary illustrative choices, not manufacturer-dedicated pairs or continuity evidence. svg.text: Proposed exterior terminals → dotted function candidates or explicit OPEN boundaries; no installed harness claim

g.title: G01: explicit design-schematic function guess to X1 optional LPT adapter · 25-position reference peripheral (shell style and gender unspecified) position 1 (Relay 1). FUNCTION GUESS ONLY, not a direct cable or a fitted conductor. Basis: X1.1 is manufacturer-labelled Relay 1; SSR1.1 is the proposed SSR 1 control 5V SWITCH contact. A relay-command function association is plausible in the computer-to-controller LPT context. A usable X1 receiving stage and compatible carrier output are inferred, not specified by those labels. Interface: DOTTED GUESS ONLY; DOTTED_CONDITIONAL_COMMAND; Hypothesis: SSR1.1 command toward X1.1; electrical stages unverified. Not a direct wire, fitted conductor or safe-to-wire approval. Checks: FIT: identify the actual controller card and optional X1 LPT adapter; match the fitted revision to one selected manufacturer schedule. The wiki machine name and USB history do not establish this hardware.; CONTACT: establish both endpoint identities, numbered-contact view, connector side, cable continuity and mating orientation. Source-order strips are not physical connector faces.; DIRECTION: identify the driving and receiving stages in powered, unpowered, reset and disconnect states. X1 has no per-contact electrical direction column.; ELECTRICAL: qualify voltage limits, thresholds, source/sink currents, output topology, active polarity, loading and necessary buffering or isolation for both exact endpoints.; RETURN: qualify reference potentials, permitted bonding, return-current paths and isolation. Repeated GND labels are not continuity measurements, dedicated pair assignments or authorization to bond PE to circuit GND.; CONTROL SOURCE: select one control source and prevent contention and backfeed from the historical USB or another host. The LPT replacement architecture is a hypothesis for this machine, not confirmed local fitment.; SAFE STATE: qualify reset and power-loss states and the separate enable/inhibit, emergency-stop, spindle and enclosure design. No dotted candidate completes a safety circuit.; R1: prove X1.1 is the selected host-command input, identify the downstream Relay 1 function, and qualify SSR1.1 switching/source topology, bias, polarity, input load, buffering and fail-off behavior. Qualify SSR1.2 or another selected return separately; the eight motor-return guesses do not complete this circuit.

G02: explicit design-schematic function guess to X1 optional LPT adapter · 25-position reference peripheral (shell style and gender unspecified) position 2 (Direction X). FUNCTION GUESS ONLY, not a direct cable or a fitted conductor. Basis: X1.2 is manufacturer-labelled X DIR; DRVX.3 is the separately named proposed X DIR output. Matching axis and function supports a dotted host-command hypothesis. The receiving direction follows the LPT architecture inference; the X1 table supplies no electrical direction or thresholds. Interface: DOTTED GUESS ONLY; DOTTED_FUNCTION; Hypothesis: DRVX.3 command toward X1.2; electrical stages unverified. Not a direct wire, fitted conductor or safe-to-wire approval. Checks: FIT: identify the actual controller card and optional X1 LPT adapter; match the fitted revision to one selected manufacturer schedule. The wiki machine name and USB history do not establish this hardware.; CONTACT: establish both endpoint identities, numbered-contact view, connector side, cable continuity and mating orientation. Repeated GND labels are not continuity measurements, dedicated pair assignments or authorization to bond PE to circuit GND.; CONTROL SOURCE: select one control source and prevent contention and backfeed from the historical USB or another host. The LPT replacement architecture is a hypothesis for this machine, not confirmed local fitment.; SAFE STATE: qualify reset and power-loss states and the separate enable/inhibit, emergency-stop, spindle and enclosure design. No dotted candidate completes a safety circuit.; M-X-DIR: identify the exact X receiving path and axis binding; qualify direction polarity and setup/hold times around the step edge.

Reassign or reject the arbitrary numeric pairing after interface qualification. Confirm the optional fourth-axis path before retaining its return choice.

g.title: X1 optional LPT adapter · 25-position reference peripheral (shell style and gender unspecified) · STEPCRAFT 2 operating manual v4 German and operating instructions v5.1 English, 2020-era family documents for sizes 210/300/420/600/840; fitted control-card revision unverified · Manufacturer v4 reference for the 210/300/420/600/840 family; X1 LPT adapter is optional and not confirmed fitted to this archived StepCraft 2/600. Each of pins 18–25 is a separate GND contact. The manual introduces X1 as the computer-to-controller LPT interface, but gives no per-pin direction, voltage, or logic threshold. The adjacent 5V VCC text has no unambiguous numbered association and is not assigned. Nineteen individually reviewed dotted drawing hypotheses are selected; the other seven X1 entries remain OPEN. All nineteen remain unqualified physical routes. The eight GND number-to-signal assignments are arbitrary illustrative choices, not manufacturer-dedicated pairs or continuity evidence. A/fourth-axis hypotheses are conditional on a selected optional drive path. The probe hypothesis is status from X1.10 toward PROBE.4; its electrical direction is unproved. Relay and probe return circuits remain separately unqualified. No installed harness or safe-to-wire approval is asserted.

svg.text: DOTTED VIOLET = FUNCTION GUESS ONLY. Paths start at the actual drawn exterior screw and end at the named machine contact. No installed continuity or direct cable is established.

OPEN / hollow contact = no SmoothieBox route selected in this study. This does not mean an electrically open circuit, unused pin or NC in the source. Source-empty, unlisted and untranscribed roles remain distinct in their labels.

REFERENCE ONLY = a named source revision, not the installed machine. Reference contacts stay OPEN unless an individually cited dotted function guess is shown. Named hardware with no contact map has an OPEN boundary, not invented '?' pins.

Paths may cross without joining; pale crossing clearance means NO JUNCTION. Multiple guesses from one screw are alternatives unless each shares an explicit FAN-OUT tag. A tagged fan-out still needs separate buffers and load validation. No return bus is

Exterior label colors: black = circuit GND; red = 3.3 V; orange = 5 V; yellow/gold = load/control feed; blue/violet/green = STEP/DIR/ENABLE. Dotted violet is an evidence state, not a reported cable color. Protective earth is not circuit GND.

DB25, DB44 and 15-contact D-sub housings are outside SmoothieBox. Contact strips preserve source order, not physical pin-row geometry. USB device, USB host, Ethernet and microSD are separate service ports.
RESEARCH DIAGRAM — NOT QUALIFIED FOR PHYSICAL WIRING. Confirm the actual carrier, machine revision, mating view, electrical interface, protection, returns and safety design before construction.
